claims.text: ALD of Pt onto ceria–zirconia combined with oxygen-vacancy enhancement produces isolated Pt atoms.
The resulting catalyst has superior catalytic activity under automotive exhaust conditions.
The resulting catalyst has superior durability under automotive exhaust conditions.
The intervention permits lower overall Pt loading.
The initial ceria–zirconia support has a moderate intrinsic density of oxygen vacancies.
Pt is to be deposited by controlled sub-monolayer ALD cycles at approximately 150 °C.
A mild reduction treatment or minor dopant addition is intended to enhance oxygen-vacancy density.
The treated catalyst is to be calcined at 500 °C in an oxygen atmosphere.
The intervention yields highly dispersed, isolated Pt atoms anchored at oxygen-vacancy sites on ceria–zirconia.
ALD allows near-atomic precision in Pt deposition.
Increasing oxygen-vacancy density strengthens the Pt–support interaction.
The strengthened Pt–support interaction reduces Pt sintering during thermal cycling.
Maintaining isolated Pt atoms increases catalytic utilization of Pt.
The catalyst will have higher catalytic activity per Pt atom than a conventionally impregnated Pt/ceria–zirconia catalyst.
The catalyst will be more durable than a conventionally impregnated Pt/ceria–zirconia catalyst.
The catalyst will reach similar or superior conversion rates at a lower overall Pt loading than the conventional-impregnation baseline.
The predicted benefits depend on the enhanced oxygen vacancies remaining effective during prolonged redox cycling.
Insufficient or degrading oxygen-vacancy enhancement can lead to Pt agglomeration and diminished catalytic performance.

contradictions.description: The stated performance baseline is conventional Pt impregnation without ALD or vacancy enhancement, but the experiment compares stabilized ALD against conventional ALD. Thus, it isolates vacancy stabilization rather than testing the full ALD-plus-stabilization intervention against the stated baseline, while the falsification rule ambiguously refers to the control as the baseline.
